name: Pixel RPG
summary: A mid-90s console RPG on a 180×320 pixel grid (6 px each): indexed 32-colour palette, Bayer-dithered skies, typed dialog boxes with a talking portrait, quest logs, battle messages and a save crystal; the topic becomes a quest.

palette.use: night: the darkest index; the ink outline of every sprite and window; the 1-pixel text shadow
navy: the middle of the dialog-box fill and of the night sky
dialog and menu text, the inner white border of windows, the brightest highlight
silver: the third window border, labels, the middle band of title type
steel: greyed-out menu items, the hero's cloak
protected red: red light (700 nm) and nothing else
protected crystal cyan: blue light, scattered sparks, the save crystal; the thread of the film
protected cyan, middle tone: blue light shading, the day sky's middle band
protected cyan, dark tone: crystal shade, the top of the day sky and of the dialog fill
protected red, dark tone
emphasised words in dialog (like an item name), sparkle stars, the sun's core
the sun's middle tone, the hero's scarf (the hero carries sunlight)
the sun's shaded edge, the scarf's shade
the night sky near the horizon, empty bar tracks, the hero's cloak shade
the bottom band of title type, the hero's cloak highlight, the molecule's shade
lit grass tops
grass
far hills, grass shade
farthest hills, hills at night
the hero's face
the hero's face in shade
boots, wood
spectrum orb: green
spectrum orb: orange
spectrum orb: violet (the palette's nearest); the dawn sky's pink band
the dawn sky between night and pink

type.case: sentence in dialog; UPPERCASE in menus and labels
type.emphasis: the keyword colour (yellow) in the same face, like an item name

banned: alpha fades, soft gradients, blur, glow, grain or scanlines: colour changes by dither or by swapping the palette in one frame
sub-pixel positions: everything sits on the 6 px grid (one native pixel)
more than the two protected colours (cyan = blue light, red = red light) carrying meaning
existing games' names, characters, fonts, window frames, logos, melodies or sound effects
a slime-shaped enemy or any well-known game creature
numbers or stats that aren't true (no invented HP or levels)
text drawn outside a window or a title screen
smooth-dome hair or helmet heads; pale clothing that reads as skin
